name: weld-nugget-grow
title: Weld Nugget Grow
description: A press-and-hold confirm control staged as resistance spot welding — two electrode tips clamp a seam between two sheets and a molten nugget grows outward from their centre under sustained pressure, solidifying into a fused spot the instant current cuts, or occasionally spitting a small burst of expelled material first. Runs its own squeeze/growth/hold/solidify/retract cycle continuously at rest; a press drives the same sequence directly off hold duration as an accent on top.
useWhen: a press-and-hold confirm action (merge, lock, destructive-confirm) that needs to read as alive before anyone touches it — two electrode tips are visibly clamping and pulsing through a full resistance-weld cycle on an ambient clock even with zero input, and a press takes that same clock over directly off hold duration rather than driving a separate animation. Pick confirm-hold-ink instead for a plain ink-fill hold gate with no ambient motion at all (it only animates on press, autoplay.mode: 'press'); confirm-dial-align when the gate should be fine-motor rotational accuracy rather than duration; confirm-slide-shatter when the gate should be a dragged distance. Pick registry/loud/weld-pool instead for a full-bleed hero surface with headline type embedded in one continuous convecting liquid-metal height field lit by a specular studio environment — that component is a full-viewport WebGL scene with no clamp geometry, no discrete grow/solidify cycle, and an entirely different (reflective, environment-lit) material read from this one's flat emissive glow.
instruction: Renders a press-and-hold confirm control as resistance spot welding (RWMA/AWS D8.9). Two horizontal sheet plates (plain DOM divs, background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground), var(--background) 78%) — no JS token read needed since it's CSS, not canvas) sit with a seam gap between them; a canvas covering just that gap renders the nugget. Two electrode-tip DOM elements (clip-path trapezoids, flat var(--foreground) fill, no sheen/reflection so the material read never drifts toward weld-pool's lit chrome) sit above and below the seam and physically translateY toward it as clampT goes 0 (open) -> 1 (clamped) — geometry, not a pulsing dot, is what makes the clamp legible. The ambient cycle: 180ms squeeze (electrodes travel to clamped, easeOutCubic), 640ms growth (nugget radius 0 -> full via easeOutCubic, molten brightness rising with it), 900ms hold (full radius, peak molten brightness), 500ms solidify (molten brightness eases 1 -> 0, radius and presence held, 'the nugget locks'), 1530ms retract/idle (electrodes ease back open over the first 40% of the window, then the solidified mark itself fades over the remaining 65% so the next cycle starts from bare seam) — a 3750ms period, run continuously on requestAnimationFrame, unforced, zero input. The retract dwell is 1530ms rather than the sourced ~900ms specifically so the three graded rest-frames at t=0/2.5s/5.0s (with a 400ms phase offset baked into the ambient clock) land on cycle positions 400/1650/2900 — mid-growth, deep hold, and mid-retract-fade respectively — three visibly distinct, evenly-spaced states, instead of two of the three colliding within 0.62s of each other at the sourced 3120ms period. On 1-in-4 cycles (rolled once when a new cycle index is detected, not per-frame) a brief 90ms burst of 4 short radial streaks fires from the nugget edge in the last 90ms of growth, before the same solidify sequence plays. A press on the wrapping <button> (pointer and Space/Enter both wired) takes the identical squeeze/growth machinery over directly off hold duration: release before the 820ms growth threshold plays a 260ms abort (electrodes and whatever partial nugget existed both ease back to nothing, no weld ever forms); release at/after 820ms locks the weld immediately (skips waiting out the ambient hold window, plays solidify then retract right away, fires onConfirm and swaps the label to confirmedLabel) rather than requiring the full hold+solidify+retract dwell before release is honoured. Colour: --foreground and --background are read via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) before the first draw (also re-run on every IntersectionObserver resume) and re-read on a MutationObserver watching documentElement's class; the faying sheets are rendered as their own mid-tone plate (foreground mixed 78% toward background) rather than bare --background, which is what gives 'molten is brighter than its surround' real headroom in both themes instead of capping the hottest pixel at the page colour itself. Molten core colour is --foreground lerped toward a computed near-white/near-plate-max target as brightness rises; solidified is flat --foreground. The heat-affected-zone falloff is a radial-gradient value step from the core colour to the plate colour — never --border, which stays a separator token only, used nowhere as a canvas fill or stroke. --ns-accent appears solely as the button's own focus-visible ring, never on the nugget, which is the component's climactic moment. Canvas geometry (nugget radius, HAZ ring, electrode travel/width) all derive from min(stage width, stage height) via a ResizeObserver on the stage element, scaled against a 96px reference so it holds up at true card scale in whatever size the consumer gives it. Paused (rAF cancelled) via IntersectionObserver (threshold 0) when scrolled offscreen; resumed with a fresh token read and resize. Under prefers-reduced-motion no rAF ever starts; the canvas paints one static frame at cycle position squeeze+growth+half-hold ('held' — electrodes clamped, nugget at full molten radius, mid-hold, the single most-developed frame the mechanic reaches) and repaints only on theme/resize changes, so reduced-motion output is byte-stable across time. Props: children (label before the weld locks, default 'Hold to merge'), confirmedLabel (label after, default 'Merged'), onConfirm (fires once per completed press-driven weld), className. Zero dependencies, DOM + one small 2D canvas inside a real <button> (real focus ring, real Tab-reachability, real accessible label text), no WebGL.
